verdictStatement: Six of the eight findings this generation set out to repair are repaired cleanly, and the two that most needed structural work — the V1 coordinator owner and the purge journal's single writer — landed exactly as their finding texts required. My own four SHOULD-FIX items from v3 are all discharged, including the roster, which now holds mechanically: 60 changed leaf paths, zero off-roster, 115 of 115 non-roster paths byte-identical. The blocker is a repair that was claimed rather than completed. Codex v3's B3 said the grant-journal carve-out contradicts SC-OPS boundedness OUTSIDE the named supersession's scope, and offered two ways out: specify a bounded lifecycle preserving durable order, or expand the supersession to cover the boundedness exception with its owner concurrence. This generation did neither. It added the fail-closed sentence — real progress on the substance — and then asserted the exception is 'inside SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL' without putting it inside: the 'of' list still contains only the three containment prohibitions, and whatIsSuperseded still opens with the word 'Only', which excludes precisely this exception. So the artifact now contains a clause that claims membership in a scope its own scope sentence denies it, and records the finding as folded with notFoldedThisSuccessor empty. That last part is what makes it a blocker rather than a drafting slip.

measurement.theFindingBeingClaimed: Codex v3 SCC-V3-B3: 'The grant-journal carve-out contradicts SC-OPS boundedness outside the named supersession's scope.' Its repair offered two routes: 'Either specify a bounded lifecycle that preserves the required durable order (including fail-closed behavior at any hard bound), or expand the named proposed supersession to cover the exact boundedness exception, its owner concurrence, scope…'
measurement.theSupersessionWasNotExpanded: /proposedSupersession/of still has exactly three entries, all containment prohibitions: 'P-005-2 not-a-grant-journal bound', 'RB-DR005-V2-A1 no-grant-or-class-admission', 'P-002-4 not-a-grant-journal bound'. ('bound' there denotes the prohibition, not boundedness.) No entry names the boundedness rule. The ownersWhoseConcurrenceIsRequired list gained the V1 coordinator for B1, not a boundedness owner.
measurement.theScopeSentenceExcludesIt: /proposedSupersession/whatIsSuperseded opens: 'ONLY the prohibition on SC-OPS containing the DR-105 grant journal, and only the matching P-002-4 prohibition on that same containment.' The word 'Only', repeated, confines the supersession to the containment prohibitions. A boundedness exception is not a containment prohibition.
measurement.andItIsNotPreservedEither: Neither surviving-force list mentions boundedness. P-005-2's surviving force is given as 'doctor's own audit record, non-authority, non-rebuildability, and never-a-peer-evidence-writer'; P-002-4's as Plan/Run exclusion, not-rebuildable, rebuildability-stays-on-P-002-3, and the completeness obligation. Both source bounds contain 'Journaled/redacted/bounded' — I verified P-005-2's text on disk — so boundedness is neither expressly superseded nor expressly preserved. It is in limbo.
measurement.theRuleAlsoLivesInLiveArchitecture: The 'journaled/redacted/bounded' rule is not only a disposition clause. It is file 04 line 205, the Operational metadata row, which this artifact carries verbatim at /stateTextCarriedVerbatim/linesVerbatim[7]: '| Operational metadata | Core lifecycle/audit/doctor owner | Excluded from Plan/Run unless an applied owner explicitly promotes a field | Journaled/redacted/bounded; backup/purge scope disclosed; never a peer evidence writer |'. File 04 appears nowhere in the 'of' list, so no supersession covers the live-architecture instance of the rule at all.
measurement.recordedAsFolded: /honestyRepairsFromV3 asserts 'SCC-V3-B3: grant-journal durable append-only / fail-closed-at-bound is the named SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL exception to SC-OPS boundedness', and /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor is [].

blockers.whyBlocker: The artifact asserts a membership that its own bytes deny. A coordinator reading the carve-out learns the boundedness exception rides SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL; a coordinator reading the supersession learns it displaces only the containment prohibitions. Both cannot be true, and the discrepancy is invisible unless the two fields are read against each other. Compounding it, the exception's live source is file 04, which no supersession names — and a CANDIDATE cannot except itself from live architecture prose by declaring an exception. This is also the exact attack the artifact's own reviewGuidance invites at entry 21 ('Attack a grant-journal unboundedness exception outside the named supersession'), and the attack succeeds. Finally, recording the finding as folded with an empty notFoldedThisSuccessor removes the coordinator's last chance to catch it: this is the first generation in this lineage where a folded-findings claim is inaccurate, and that claim is the mechanism the whole succession discipline rests on.
blockers.whatIsNotWrong: The engineering position is right and I am not asking for it to change. An append-only monotonic ordering journal cannot be dropped or bounded away without destroying the property DR-105's linearization depends on, and 'fail-closed rather than drop order' is the correct behavior at any imposed bound. The defect is entirely about which instrument authorizes the exception.
blockers.minimumRepair: Take one of Codex's two routes and complete it. Preferred: expand the supersession — add a fourth 'of' entry naming the SC-OPS boundedness rule as it appears in file 04 line 205 and in P-005-2 / P-002-4; amend whatIsSuperseded so the 'Only' clause admits it (or restate the scope as two displacements, containment and boundedness); and name the owner whose concurrence the boundedness exception requires, which for the file 04 instance is the DR-124 owner set rather than the disposition owners. Alternatively, drop the 'inside SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL' attribution and carry the fail-closed sentence as a stated residual that DR-124's closure must resolve. Either way, correct /honestyRepairsFromV3 and list SCC-V3-B3 in notFoldedThisSuccessor if it is not fully folded.

coordinatorNote: One blocker, and it is one field wide — but I would not let it through as clerical, for a reason specific to this lineage. Every generation here has been governed by two claims a reviewer relies on: the closed roster, and notFoldedThisSuccessor. The roster claim is now perfect and I verified it mechanically. The folded-findings claim is, for the first time, wrong: SCC-V3-B3 is listed as repaired and half of it is. The substance of that half is genuinely good — fail-closed rather than drop order is the right answer — so the repair is close. What is missing is that the supersession was never actually expanded to hold the exception, while the carve-out says it was, and the word 'Only' in whatIsSuperseded is what makes the two irreconcilable. There is also a question underneath it the coordinator may want to settle directly: the boundedness rule lives in file 04, not only in the two dispositions, and nothing in this artifact's supersession machinery reaches live architecture prose. If DR-124's closure genuinely needs an exception to a file 04 class rule, that is a larger act than superseding two preview dispositions, and it should be named as such. S-1 is minor and mechanical. I did not read the other current v4 reviewer, did not edit the subject, file 08, or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, did not apply SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL, did not mint a D-096 (A) grant, and did not commit.
